english.notes:
(i) See section 24 of the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 for alternative verdict.
(ii) The 'specified limit' for each drug is listed in the Drug Driving (Specified Limits) (England and Wales) Regulations 2014.
(iii) Section 5A(3) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that It is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this section to show that –
(a) the specified controlled drug had been prescribed or supplied to him / her for medical or dental purposes,
(b) he / she took the drug in accordance with any directions given by the person by whom the drug was prescribed or supplied, and with any accompanying instructions (so far as consistent with any such directions) given by the manufacturer or distributor of the drug, and (c) his / her possession of the drug immediately before taking it was not unlawful under section 5(1) of the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 (restriction of possession of controlled drugs) because of an exemption in regulations made under section 7 of that Act (authorisation of activities otherwise unlawful under foregoing provisions).
(iv) Section 5A(4) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 provides that the defence in section 5A(3) is not available if his / her actions were –
(a) contrary to any advice, given by the person by whom the drug was prescribed or supplied, about the amount of time that should elapse between taking the drug and driving a motor vehicle, or
(b) contrary to any accompanying instructions about that matter (so far as consistent with any such advice) given by the manufacturer or distributor of the drug.
(v) Where the proportion of more than one specified drug is found to be over the limit, CPS advise that a separate charge be brought in respect of each drug.
(vi) Note that 'Cannabis' is not one of the specified controlled drugs. 'Cannabis' is a generic name for a plant and products produced from it and cannot be measured. However, the active ingredient that makes a person likely to be unfit to drive, that can be measured, is delta-9-tetrahydrocannibinol (sometimes known as THC). It is this that has been specified in the Regulations and this that should be written in the charge.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Note:
In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to fifty one weeks is to be read as a reference to six months

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
